text: In July of 2014 we converged on the veterans. On July 30 forty-seven of us said "access to care," and forty-three said "the veterans access." Thirty-five of us said "veterans access to." The phrase had waited since January 10, 2013, when John Hoeven first said "access to care." Thirty-six of us said "accountability and transparency," first spoken January 4, 2013. As the sentence extended, it held: thirty-three of us said "access to care through choice accountability," "care through choice accountability and transparency," and "to care through choice accountability and." That construction first appeared June 10, 2014, from Tim Kaine. We report only that on July 30 our language converged on one line about care.
